issues.label: 1a, 3a, 7a, 10a
issues.detail: Questions 1a, 3a, 7a, and 10a are identical (name two major trade routes). This constitutes exact repetition across four separate assessment sections, reducing assessment validity and suggesting copy-paste errors rather than progressive learning.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: ask about specific characteristics of routes, regional impacts, or comparative analysis (e.g., 'Compare the Silk Road and Trans-Saharan Trade in terms of goods exchanged').

issues.label: 1b, 3b, 7b, 10b
issues.detail: Questions 1b, 3b, 7b, and 10b are identical (Silk Road and Buddhism spread). Four exact repetitions of the same question across the assessment undermines differentiation and depth of learning.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: ask about different religions (Islam via Trans-Saharan), different goods, or different cultural impacts (e.g., 'How did the Trans-Saharan Trade spread Islam to West Africa?').

issues.label: 2a, 5a, 9a
issues.detail: Questions 2a, 5a, and 9a all calculate caravan speed using identical methodology (distance/time = 50 km/day). Three repetitions of the same calculation with same numerical answer reduces assessment variety.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: calculate different metrics (e.g., daily cost per km, goods per day, time to cover specific segments) or use different distance/time combinations.

issues.label: 4a, 6a, 8a
issues.detail: Questions 4a, 6a, and 8a are identical (calculate Timbuktu-Genoa distance: 1,500 + 1,200 = 2,700 km). Three exact repetitions of the same calculation.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: calculate different route segments, compare multiple routes, or calculate time given speed.

issues.label: 4c, 5c, 6c, 9c
issues.detail: Questions 4c, 5c, 6c, and 9c all ask to 'Describe the role of caravans in Long Distance Trade between Mali and Genoa' with nearly identical model answers. Four repetitions of the same question.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: ask about caravan organization, security measures, specific goods transported, or comparison with maritime trade.

issues.label: 2b, 5b, 9b
issues.detail: Questions 2b, 5b, and 9b all ask 'Explain why the caravan took [60/54/54] days' with similar model answers citing terrain, weather, and rest stops. Three near-identical questions.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: ask about specific obstacles (bandits, water scarcity), seasonal timing, or comparison of travel times across different routes.

issues.label: 4b, 6b, 8b
issues.detail: Questions 4b, 6b, and 8b all ask 'Explain how the trade route facilitated cultural exchange between Mali and Genoa' with similar model answers. Three repetitions.
issues.correction: Vary subsequent instances: ask about specific cultural impacts (religious conversion, architectural influence, linguistic borrowing) or compare cultural exchange across different routes.

issues.label: 8b
issues.detail: Marking criteria requires 'historically plausible example of cultural exchange' but model answer provides vague examples ('introduction of new agricultural techniques and Islamic learning') without specific evidence. Criteria demand specificity that model answer lacks.
issues.correction: Model answer should provide concrete example: 'Islamic learning from Mali influenced Mediterranean scholarship' or 'Mali's architectural styles influenced Mediterranean design' with specific details.

review.summary: Assessment contains severe repetition issues: questions 1a/3a/7a/10a identical; 1b/3b/7b/10b identical; 2a/5a/9a identical; 4a/6a/8a identical; 4c/5c/6c/9c identical; 2b/5b/9b similar; 4b/6b/8b similar. One marking criterion (8b) mismatches model answer. Recommend substantial restructuring to ensure assessment variety and validity.
